title: Risk Registry Schema
description: SSOT for risk classification, scoring rules, and dependency gate policies (H5).

risks.description: The registered risks themselves: which concrete actions are banned or need review (H5-3's actual question). risk_tiers and risk_scoring only say how to CLASSIFY an action — until this list existed there was nowhere to record the classifications anyone had made, so a file named 'risk registry' registered nothing and each reviewer kept their own list. PORTAL NOTE: H5-3 counts whatever `risk_registry.action_path` in the Portal's criteria catalogue points at, which defaults to 'risk_scoring.base_scores'; set it to 'risks' if you want these entries counted instead of the scoring table.

id.description: Stable handle for the risk, so a review or an approval record can cite it and still mean the same thing after the list is reordered.

action.description: The action being registered, in the vocabulary you already classify by — a risk_scoring.base_scores action_type, or a tool name from the tool registry. One or the other consistently; a registry that mixes 'deploy_production' with 'the deploy script' cannot be matched against anything by machine.

tier.description: Severity, from the same closed set as risk_tiers[].level and the tool registry's risk_level. The enum can only check the value is a real level — it cannot check that YOUR risk_tiers actually declares that level, so keep the two lists together.

requires_approval.description: Does this specific action need a human before it runs? Required, because it is the entry's whole point: 'bị cấm hoặc cần review' is unanswerable for a risk that records no verdict. Tier alone does not say it — tier gates on score, this records the decision taken about this action. DECLARATIVE: approval-gate.ps1 decides from risk_scoring/risk_tiers, so setting this true does not by itself block anything.

owner.description: Who answers for this risk. A name here is what turns an unmitigated entry into someone's task instead of a shared shrug.

mitigation.description: The control that makes the residual risk acceptable, and honestly — if the mitigation is 'we intend to', say that, because an aspirational entry read as a live control is worse than an empty field.
